result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers group the terms the same way and choose the same standards (Appointment, Sign in/Sign out, Practitioner, Member). Both also keep separate removal verbs according to what each action actually does. B wins narrowly: its single table covers every term, it ranks what to fix first, and it explicitly allows a deliberate, different word for the patient-facing side. B loses some credit on rubric item 2 because it spends several bullets on the Members decision, including a compliance concern about using 'patient'. A is more concise, but it doesn't really address audiences using different words on purpose. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers group the terms the same way, choose Appointment, Sign in/Sign out and Practitioner, and correctly keep separate removal verbs, with Cancel appointment and Keep appointment as the dialog pair. B handles Members better: it treats the founder's decision as settled and turns it into a practical step, a search of every string. A goes further and suggests 'patient' may be needed for compliance, which starts to reopen the decision. A gets credit for saying staff and patients can deliberately see different words for the same person, but B is tighter overall, separates what to fix from what to keep more clearly, and raises Archive for clinical records.
